subject: Vulnerability assurance Q&A — SBOM inventory & pen test summary
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@bluecrest.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vulnerability assurance details request for RFP

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As part of our procurement packet I need a few specific items expanded for our security review team so we can clear the vendor checklist:

1) A high-level SBOM inventory export that shows component names, versions, and whether it is first- or third-party. Prefer CSV.
2) Summary report of most recent external pen test (scope, critical/medium findings, remediation status).
3) SAST/DAST cadence and which scanners are used (commercial/open-source), plus how you validate fixes before deploy.
4) Patch SLAs for urgent/vulnerability/backport patches and how rollouts interact with customer-dedicated deployments.

Can you share the items above or point me to the file in your assurance package? We have an internal cutoff for Q&A on Thursday morning PST.

Thanks,
Jordan Price
Security Program Manager
Bluecrest Capital

---

Note: our compliance team will likely follow up with a couple clarifying Qs after they review your documents.
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@bluecrest.com>
Cc: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@bluecrest.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vulnerability assurance details request for RFP

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear list. Attaching an SBOM export (CSV) and our most recent pen-test summary (redacted for customer-sensitive findings). I also attached a short SAST/DAST process overview and a matrix for our patch SLAs. See attachments: redwood_sbom_inventory_2027-03.csv, pen-test-summary-2026.pdf, sast-dast-process-overview.pdf, patch-sla-matrix.xlsx.

Quick hits while the team reviews:
- SBOM: generated per-release from our build pipeline; includes direct deps + transitive dependencies. We mark components with commercial licenses in the CSV.
- Pen test: external vendor performed an infrastructure + web-app test in Nov 2026; critical findings were 0, two medium items (now closed), remainder low/accepted. We include remediation tickets and dates in the summary.
- SAST/DAST: we run SAST on every PR using a commercial scanner (Snyk/ShiftLeft hybrid) plus open-source static checks; DAST runs nightly against staging and on-demand for major releases. Findings go into Jira and require a security reviewer and QA verification before merge.
- Patch SLAs: emergency security patch (P0) — target 24–72 hours to mitigation on Hosted; 72–168 hours for Dedicated/Private depending on customer change window (we coordinate with the customer runbook). Non-critical patches follow our standard fortnightly cadence. The matrix has more nuance per OS and runtime.

If you want, I can redact anything further for public disclosure and produce a short addendum that maps each SBOM component to whether we produce a CVE monitor/watch.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Senior Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Soojin — quick follow-ups from our control owners:

1) For the SAST/DAST statement, can you confirm which findings are configured as 'fail-build' vs 'ticket-to-fix'? We need the policy language for our procurement checklist.
2) Regarding the patch SLAs for Dedicated/Private, do you have a standard customer change window template you can share? We want to understand escalation if a P0 is discovered outside the customer's maintenance window.

If possible please provide the exact policy lines we can paste into our internal vendor risk intake (one paragraph for each item above).

Thanks —
Alex Cheng
Director, Vendor Risk
Bluecrest Capital
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Suggested reply copy and templates for Bluecrest

Soojin / team —

Draft language below you can paste to Alex. I attached a short change-window template and our escalation playbook (internal) — will redact the internal-only portions before we send: see patch-sla-matrix.xlsx referenced earlier.

SAST/DAST policy (suggested wording):
"SAST checks are enforced at build time; critical and high-severity SAST findings configured as 'fail-build' must be remediated prior to merge. Medium/low findings are triaged into our backlog and tracked via Jira; they require a security reviewer to accept the risk or create a remediation ticket. DAST runs against staging and critical/high findings that indicate exploitable vectors are blocked from release until a mitigating change is deployed and verified by QA and security."

Patch SLA & change-window (suggested wording):
"For Hosted deployments, Redwood targets mitigation actions for P0 security vulnerabilities within 24–72 hours. For Dedicated and Private deployments, Redwood will coordinate an emergency maintenance window with the customer's designated technical contact; typical mitigation target for P0 is within 72–168 hours depending on agreed change-window constraints. Redwood's escalation process (outlined in the attached playbook) includes a 24/7 on-call rotation and a documented rollback plan; we will offer binary packages, migration scripts, or hotfixes as appropriate to minimize customer impact."

Notes: if Bluecrest requires guaranteed patching within 72 hours for Private, we can discuss a contractual SLA amendment (would be scoped as an enterprise add-on).

If you want, I can create a redacted pen-test findings table that maps each finding to Jira ID and remediation date (we should keep customer-only proof-of-fix artifacts for the final submission).

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security Engr Solutions
Redwood Inference
